newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks end mostly up, seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks end mostly up, seen stabilising.

text.p: Croatian stocks opened the week mostly higher in lively trade on Tuesday, with food concern Podravka extending last week's gains, but traders foresaw some corrections in prices this week.

"I expect mild growth, although I think some prices went up too high and may need to be corrected," Zoran Ilic of Consult Invest brokerage said. "We can maybe hope for another investment wave before summer and if not, nothing major will happen before the autumn."

By the close, eleven of sixteen active stocks rose, three fell and two were flat on a higher volume of 11,597 shares and turnover almost doubled to 6.7 million kuna. Food company Podravka led the gainers, adding 14 kuna or five percent to 290 on volume of 2,543 shares after a gradual rise last week.
"Investors have finally gone for Podravka more strongly," Ilic said, predicting the stock would reach 300 kuna by the end of the week on higher volumes.
But Damir Cikotic of Faktor brokerage from the Adriatic port of Split said spectacular growth was not on the cards despite great foreign demand.

Another popular food stock, chocolate maker Kras, inched up six kuna to 400, trading 1,053 shares. Cikotic said its price would stagnate as "buyers were nervous over delays in talks about foreign investment to modernise production".
Electrical manufacturer Koncar shed 60 kuna to 810 on a modest volume of 50, but brokers said the stock had a bright future as one of the next to be listed in London.
"Zagrebacka is involved in arranging the issue, which means its chances are substantial," said Cikotic.
"The summer season is already knocking on our door and things are not likely to move up before September," he said, adding blue chips might manage to fight off the summer lull.
Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka was on the losing side, sliding 40 kuna to 2,070 on moderate volume of 1,000.
The bank later announced it expected 17 percent balance sheet growth this year with a 12 percent rise in the parent bank's net profit.
Another blue chip, drugs company Pliva, was the day's most active stock, adding six kuna to 464 and trading 3,019 shares.
Cikotic described both market heavyweights as stable and likely to keep up slow and steady growth throughout the summer.
Fully-listed Varazdinska Banka rose 15 kuna to 205 on moderate volume of 190 units.
Four of five active hoteliers were among the gainers. Jadranturist with 1,211 shares sold was the most active. It added eight kuna to 250. Istarturist rose ten kuna to 170 on volume of 441.
"This should be the first proper tourist season after the war and I think hoteliers are simply bound to grow," said Cikotic.
